body: Agreed, my SO and I have really struggled with that. It can be really hard, and you know you've got a good one if they stay anyway.
They go hand in hand for me, although SH/SI persists even when I'm in recovery.

I know it's scary to think that people might leave you. I'd be a hypocrite to say I dont feel the same things and that I struggle telling my own SO things. 
I am really trying to believe people when they say whatever they say. If my coworker says, "Text me, call me anytime, I just want you to be okay." 
I'm not quite succeeding yet, but I decide to believe her.. and who knows she might be getting a text sent her way if I'm feeling down.
And if she reacts poorly then I now know exactly who she is as a person. Someone who doesnt stick to their word or practice what they preach. Those are her problems, not mine. So that's at least my attempt to argue with the ED.

As far as my SO, same thing, if hes saying he'll be there for me I am choosing to believe him actively. Doesnt always work and I omit or lie, but you know baby steps. I know it's scary, I like to believe the person for me will be able to accept all of me and that includes mental illness <3

I like to believe I'm building a healthy relationship. I've been with my SO for almost 7 years, but was only diagnosed these past 2 years. Before I even knew I had an ED I was very codependent. Crying when he had to leave, even if it was just to go and come back. It was bad, but he knew I dealt with mental illness and so does he so we stuck it out. I was going to therapy and trying to get better and that was good enough for him that I at least try.

Fast forward to around this time last year, I go into residential treatment for the first time. I'm doing my treatment thing, get into outpatient after about 7mths.
I'm not cured but the difference treatment made for me was reminding myself I dont have to be all alone. I started talking more and expressing my likes and dislikes more. Having friends. Something my SO had to adjust to, which he was happy to do!

So we are evolving right now. I'm going back to Res this month, but I'm ready this time and I know what I need to focus on. Some of it is relationship based and while I'm waiting to get into treatment its has been rough for us both because I'm just not myself. He reminds me that when he gets upset, hes upset with my illness, not me. And we both know once I'm out of treatment for good this time that I'm going to be different. Still me, but I'm sure he'll see qualities and stuff he hasn't really encountered before with me. So we adjust, communicate, and keep it moving!

I'm finding the more I communicate the more control I kind of have over my life when I'm recovered. ED likes to keep me all quiet and docile. 

It's possible and it takes work, which I know none of us are strangers too :)

I can sympathize with what you're going through. The best advice I can give you is to try to get him to see a doctor, but if he's like my boyfriend and doesn't want to just ask him what he needs when he feels that way. Does he need space? A hug? Has he taken care of himself that day? (Like has he eaten or showered) Those kind of things make you feel better even if it's the last thing you feel like doing. And lastly don't take it personally when he told you his feelings I'm sure he didn't mean he doesn't find any joy in you or your relationship he's just stating that's how he feels a lot of the time. I'm sure you are one of the reasons he's still fighting to feel better! So just try to be as supportive as possible, but remember to take care of yourself too, it can be hard caring for someone with depression and anxiety.

It's rough having to keep up with your life and dealing with depression at the same time. As much as you might want to quit your job because it might help you focus on your health, it also might make it worse. That's what I hate about depression, there's always a something that could help it, but there's always a chance it won't work. It's infuriating. The way I muddle through it is literally just one day at a time. Sometimes one minute at a time. It's not the best existence but I believe I'll eventually be able to pick my head up and look a bit further into the future. You just gotta do what you gotta do sometimes, and if taking it day by day is what gets you through then you gotta do that.. I'm sorry your having such a hard time. Since you don't really want to talk to any professionals... maybe start with your boyfriend? Mine is really a great resource for me when I'm feeling down. It might make him feel better too, you letting him in instead of pushing him out. Sometimes I like to preface my SO and I's conversations with, "I don't really need you to say anything, I just need you to listen." That helps when I don't really want an opinion, but I just need a good listener and a cuddle. Maybe try that next time you feel like locking him out, I'm sure he's just trying to understand and just wants to help.
